Most dudes I know would sooner kick a puppy than admit that the character is a shitty person who needs a redemption arc before being portrayed as a hero, and movie folk even less so.

But there's a good story in there. It's a bit like Iron Man evolving from being this self-involved douchebag to deciding to help others, to learning to work with others and accomplish great things. Start the character as this awful person who is really just getting his rocks off, and have other characters like Superman, Wonder Woman, etc. show him that his approach is self-defeating and not actually helping anyone. Then as the scale of threats grow bigger and beyond Gotham, the character starts to realize what he can do to actually make positive changes and uses his fortune to do stuff like build factories and bankroll the Justice League.

You can still have him brood, and be the badass loner of the team, and have "issues," and be the coolest guy for using gadgets instead of having innate superpowers. You can also have him go back to Gotham every now and again to deal with a supervillain or a crime family that rose up in his absence. You can even use a "safer" more gentrified Gotham to show how and why the character would enlist teenage/young adult sidekicks and train them to watch the city while he's gone.
